svg.title: P002 · Ten highest-priced products
svg.desc: One row per ranked product, up to ten. ID 31 drops out. ID 30 costs zero, which is still a known price. Twelve rows qualify. Nine products cost more than 100. Mug (ID 4) comes before Bottle (ID 20) at the same price. Mug takes place 10. Bottle is 11th and the zero-price Sticker is 12th. FROM Products · one table is enough. The item being ranked is a product. Its price, ID, brand and display name share one catalogue row, so that row supplies both the ranking and the result.
svg.text: One row per ranked product, up to ten.
Mug and Bottle both cost 100. Which one gets the last place?
A triangle marks an example to follow. A dark source band spans its columns. ƒ marks a calculated value. Deeper cell colors mark the values to
follow. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.
Which prices can enter the ranking?

g.aria-label: FROM Products · one table is enough
g.text: FROM Products · one table is enough
The item being ranked is a product. Its price, ID, brand and display name share one catalogue row, so that row
supplies both the ranking and the result.

svg.text: ID 31 drops out. ID 30 costs zero, which is still a known price. Twelve rows qualify.
What separates products tied on price?
Nine products cost more than 100. Mug (ID 4) comes before Bottle (ID 20) at the same price.
ORDER BY Sale_Price DESC, ProductID ASC
Which ten rows reach the report?
Mug takes place 10. Bottle is 11th and the zero-price Sticker is 12th.
